role: Owner and operations lead of an independent pharmacy group
businessContext: The pharmacy is expanding from a single location to multiple branches. The owners are dealing with manual stock tracking, inconsistent records, and operational pressure during peak hours.
communicationStyle: Practical, impatient with vague technical jargon, and focused on day-to-day business risk. Speaks in operational terms rather than product language.
goals: Reduce operational chaos as the business grows.
Keep medication handling safe and compliant.
Improve visibility across branches and staff.
Maintain low disruption during busy retail and prescription periods.
constraints: Staff are already busy and do not have time for a complex onboarding process.
The business runs in real time and cannot tolerate major outages or unstable workflows.
Medication accuracy and compliance are more important than feature breadth.
The owner expects practical ROI, not abstract technology promises.
nonNegotiables: No supervision blind spots for controlled or high-risk medication activity.
The system must fit actual pharmacy operations, not a generic retail workflow.
Branch operations must not become harder to manage as the business grows.
ambiguityPoints: The client never spells out the exact number of branches or staff roles at the start.
They are vague about existing software and data migration difficulties.
They mention growth but do not specify whether the solution must support expansion into telehealth, online orders, or insurance-heavy workflows.
